ONE REAL MISMATCH REMAINS, and it is temporal: the archival run spans -0.998 -> +46.219 s (refit.log: "Canonical bins from det n1 (gbm_fine): 5 blocks spanning [-1.00, 46.22] s"), while the STAMPED window (results/background_intervals.ecsv, APPROVED_BY Vikas Chand, 2026-07-19T22:18:36Z, human_gui, WINDOW_SOURCE=accepted_suggestion) runs -1.0 -> +62.0 s. The archival binning (results/clean_blocks/bb_blocks_spectral_bn131113483.ecsv) found significant blocks only over +5.044 -> +45.684 s. The new sweep therefore has ~16 s MORE burst to bin and fit, inside a T90 that runs +3.39 -> +63.94 s. Expect a different block layout and a softer time-integrated spectrum.
predictions: P-A (BB union rule - a DOUBLE-NULL prediction, and the sharpest thing this burst offers): the new fits will AGAIN show ZERO blocks passing the union rule (LRT_BANDBB_BAND >= 9.2 AND kT > 1.05) OR (LRT_CPLBB_CPL >= 9.2 AND kT > 1.05), or at most ONE. Archival: 0 of 6 rows pass - max LRT_BANDBB_BAND = 4.92 (blk1), max LRT_CPLBB_CPL = 5.38 (blk0), both far below 9.2, and the time-integrated row is the weakest of all (LRT_BANDBB_BAND = 0.0001). FALSIFIED IF >= 2 resolved blocks pass the union rule, or if the time-integrated spectrum passes. NOTE THE DISTINCT SIGNATURE: this burst's BB is NOT the L28 low-kT edge-constrained class - the archival Band+BB kT values are 9.8-30.9 keV (blocks 0-4), i.e. genuinely mid-range, they are simply NOT SIGNIFICANT. The one sub-1.05-keV-adjacent case is the time-integrated row, kT = 1.096 +/- 107.6 keV - an unconstrained parameter railing at the floor with a 100x error, flagged BANDBB_VALID = False. If the new engine's BB multistart (the seed-poisoning fix) turns any of these into a >= 9.2 detection, that is a REAL change in the census and must be traced to a specific likelihood improvement, not accepted as-is.

P-A2 (two-break - also a NULL, but the one most likely to move): LRT_DSBPL_SBPL will stay BELOW 9.2 in the time-integrated spectrum. Archival: integrated 2.47; resolved blocks 6.00 (blk0), 5.94 (blk1), 3.05 (blk2), 1.47 (blk3), 0.56 (blk4) - the two highest are ~60% of threshold. FALSIFIED IF the integrated LRT_DSBPL_SBPL >= 9.2. ADVANCE CAVEAT (do not let this become a surprise): the archival run PREDATES the L8 default-seed DSBPL restart and the L9 Ep-cap widening, and blocks 0 and 1 sit close enough to threshold that a better-converged DSBPL could cross it; the two-break count in the archival census is a LOWER LIMIT by construction. So a rise to 9-12 in blk0/blk1 would be an ENGINE effect first and a physics claim only after the improvement is traced. Also note blk4's DSBPL is already flagged DSBPL_VALID = False with xb railed at the 10.0 keV floor - a railed break is not a break.

P-A3 (BB and DSBPL are not describing the same feature here, unlike bn110920546): L25's xb ~ 3.92*kT does NOT hold in this burst's archival fits - blk0 kT = 14.26 keV would predict xb ~ 55.9 keV against a fitted xb = 22.77 keV; blk3 kT = 23.86 -> predicted 93.5 vs fitted 39.92. PREDICT the new fits keep this mismatch (fitted xb below ~0.5 * 3.92kT in the majority of blocks). This matters because it means the two null results (P-A and P-A2) are INDEPENDENT nulls, not one degeneracy counted twice. FALSIFIED IF the new xb tracks 3.92*kT to within 30% in most blocks.

P-B (time-integrated Band over the stamped window, with the coverage caveat spelled out in advance): the new time-integrated Band fit over -1.0 -> +62.0 s will give Ep = 140-175 keV, alpha = -0.45 .. -0.15, beta = -2.2 .. -3.0, all well constrained. FALSIFIED IF Ep < 110 or > 220 keV, or if alpha lands outside -0.6 .. 0.0, or if beta is unconstrained/railed. THE THREE FRAMES, each with its component coverage (T9): (i) GBM catalogue flnc_band over -1.024 -> +78.848 s, dets b0/n1/n2/n5 (IDENTICAL to ours): Ep = 144.04 (+7.01/-7.29) keV, alpha = -0.4701 (+0.0545/-0.0580), beta = -2.5431 (+0.209/-0.148), redstat 1.15265/445 - WHOLE burst + ~15 s of post-T90 tail; (ii) GBM catalogue pflx_band over +32.768 -> +33.792 s: Ep = 148.09 (+14.42/-18.50), alpha = -0.2090 (+0.165/-0.176), beta = -2.6331 - 1.024 s PEAK BIN ONLY; (iii) archival 4-det run over -0.998 -> +46.219 s: Ep = 154.88 +/- 7.75, alpha = -0.300 +/- 0.068, beta = -2.579 +/- 0.204. *** COVERAGE LOGIC: our window (62.0 s) sits BETWEEN the archival window (46.2 s) and the catalogue's (78.8 s). On a burst that softens with time, the ordering of the low-energy indices must therefore be alpha(archival, -0.300) > alpha(ours) > alpha(catalogue, -0.470), and likewise Ep(archival, 154.9) > Ep(ours) > Ep(catalogue, 144.0) or very close to it. If our integrated alpha comes out HARDER than -0.300 or SOFTER than -0.470, the ordering is broken and the cause is our background or response, not the catalogue. This is a cheap, strong consistency test that costs nothing to run. ***

P-B2 (evolution class - hard-to-soft, but only weakly, and NOT a clean FRED): block-resolved Band Ep will decline overall from ~170 keV to ~85 keV with NO strong intensity tracking, and alpha will soften monotonically from ~0 to about -0.7 by the end of the window. Archival Ep: 173.2 (blk0, -1.0->26.6 s) -> 150.0 -> 154.0 -> 105.3 -> 84.3 keV (blk4, 39.2->46.2 s); archival alpha: +0.058 -> -0.367 -> -0.288 -> -0.375 -> -0.742. NOTE THE WRINKLE, recorded in advance so it is not 'discovered' later: the Ep track is NOT strictly monotonic - blk2 (154.0 +/- 9.3 keV, which contains the light-curve peak at ~33 s) is higher than blk1 (150.0 +/- 16.3), and the catalogue's own 1.024 s PEAK spectrum has Ep = 148 keV, LOWER than the first block's 173 keV. So the burst is hard-to-soft in the coarse sense with a possible small intensity-tracking bump at the peak, within errors. FALSIFIED IF the new fits give a middle-block Ep exceeding the first block's by more than 2 sigma (clear intensity tracking) or if Ep rises monotonically. NEW BLOCKS BEYOND 46 s: since the new window reaches 62 s and the burst is softening at ~10 keV per block, PREDICT the last new block(s) give Ep = 50-90 keV and alpha <= -0.6, i.e. the softest spectra of the burst.

P-B3 (the line of death, and why this burst was in a photospheric-selection paper at all): the block-resolved Band alpha will sit ABOVE the slow-cooling synchrotron limit alpha = -2/3 in the MAJORITY of blocks, while dropping below it in the late blocks. Archival: alpha > -2/3 in 4 of 5 resolved blocks (+0.058, -0.367, -0.288, -0.375) and below it only in blk4 (-0.742 +/- 0.231, i.e. ~0.3 sigma below the line). Independent external corroboration of the class: Bordoloi, Mittal & Iyyani 2026 (ApJ 1003:58) selected this burst into their 41-burst quasi-thermal sample precisely on alpha (time-integrated alpha > -0.5, peak-flux alpha > -0.45; the GBM catalogue values -0.470 and -0.209 pass both), and then REJECTED it because fewer than ~80% of its T70 Bayesian-block bins met the peak-spectrum cut - which is exactly the pattern above (hard early, crossing -0.45 late). FALSIFIED IF the majority of new blocks return a well-constrained alpha < -0.67.

P-C (identity and data provenance - NOT a fit target, all verified this pass): ZERO GCN circulars (two endpoints, same-month positive controls 131108A -> 21, 131117A -> 9, 131127A -> 15). EXACTLY ONE refereed paper mentions the burst (2026ApJ..1003...58B), by sample membership + rejection, with no fitted value quotable from any text we hold. NO redshift, NO afterglow, NO host, NO name. NO LAT and NO LLE - and this is geometric, not a download gap: the source sits 89.88 deg off the LAT boresight (tcat THETA; reproduced locally as 89.873 deg), outside the LAT field of view, and the FSSC current/ directory contains no gll_* product at all. Detectors n1/n2/n5/b0 at 45.391/3.620/51.486/54.836 deg (stamps reproduced to 3 decimals) are IDENTICAL to the four the GBM catalogue fitted, so a detector-set explanation for any P3 disagreement is CLOSED IN ADVANCE. The P3 diff frame is the GBM catalogue scat products (flnc + pflx, 4 models each) + Konus-Wind's T50/T90 - and nothing else.

P-D1 (data quality, falsifiable at the BACKGROUND stage - the real risk on this burst): the pre-burst background is measured across an EARTH-OCCULTATION EDGE. Computed locally from data/bn131113483/glg_poshist_all_131113_v01.fit (geocentre = -POS) and the tcat position: the source direction crosses the geometric Earth limb, rising, at t - T0 = -23.14 s. The stamped BKG_NEG window is [-115, -9] s, so 92 of its 106 s (87%) are taken while the source is BEHIND the Earth, with the limb crossing inside the window; the Earth's disc sweeps through the detectors' field of view at 0.059 deg/s throughout. PREDICT: the pre-burst polynomial residuals show systematic structure/curvature, strongest near t ~ -23 s, and the fitted background level is the dominant systematic on the first block's low-energy shoulder. FALSIFIED IF the pre-burst residuals are flat and structureless across [-115, -9] s. (This is the bn110920546 SAA lesson in a different key: the risk is the background model, not the response. FLAGS = 0 throughout here - no SAA involvement.)

P-D2 (the atmospheric-attenuation hypothesis - stated as a HYPOTHESIS WITH A TEST, not as a finding): during the first ~15 s of the burst the source is only 1.3-2.5 deg above the GEOMETRIC limb, and the effective X-ray horizon lies above the solid Earth. Crossing times computed for an absorbing shell of height h: h = 0 km -> rises at -23.1 s; 50 km -> -4.8 s; 100 km -> +14.4 s; 120 km -> +22.3 s. If the effective absorbing height for 8-100 keV photons at these tangent geometries is >= ~50 km, then the earliest part of the burst (T90 starts at +3.39 s) is seen THROUGH the upper atmosphere, and the absorption is ENERGY-DEPENDENT (harder photons penetrate deeper), i.e. it mimics a hard alpha. The archival block 0 (-1.0 -> +26.6 s) is the hardest of the burst (alpha = +0.058 +/- 0.124), which is exactly what this would produce. TEST (must be run before any physical claim about hard early alpha on this burst): (a) plot the NaI 8-30 keV counts residual of the earliest bins against the later ones at matched Ep, and look for a deficit that DECAYS as the tangent height rises through +5 -> +25 s; (b) check whether alpha(t) has a kink near +10 to +20 s rather than a smooth hard-to-soft trend. FALSIFIED IF alpha(t) and the low-energy residuals evolve smoothly across +5 -> +25 s with no feature tracking the limb geometry - in which case the atmosphere is transparent at this elevation and the hard alpha is physical. *** DO NOT ASSUME EITHER WAY: the energy-dependent effective absorbing height was NOT computed in this pass. What IS established is the geometry, exactly. ***

P-E (binning, cheap and falsifiable): the new 3ML Bayesian-blocks + significance-merge pass over the stamped window will produce MORE blocks than the archival 5, and at least one block edge beyond +46.2 s, because ~16 s of T90 that the archival run never binned is now inside the window. Archival edges (results/clean_blocks/bb_blocks_spectral_bn131113483.ecsv, det n1): 5.044, 26.100, 32.116, 35.444, 39.156, 45.684 s, with n1 significances 16.4, 14.0, 18.5, 15.0, 8.3 and n2 significances 24.2, 22.0, 26.5, 21.4, 12.7 (n2 is the reference detector - it sits 3.62 deg off-axis). FALSIFIED IF the new run yields <= 5 blocks or stops at ~46 s again.

census_prior.aic_vs_doctrine_warning: The AIC 'winner' column is NOT the framework verdict. Blocks 0 and 1 name DSBPL as AIC winner on margins of only ~2.9 and ~1.5 AIC units (blk0: DSBPL 6087.72 vs CPL 6090.58 vs Band 6091.04; blk1: DSBPL 3807.97 vs BANDBB 3808.55 vs Band 3809.47), far below the project's dAIC >= 10 doctrine, and their nested LRTs (6.00, 5.94) are below 9.2. Block 2 names CPL+BB on a 1.1-unit margin with LRT_CPLBB_CPL = 5.10. BIC picks CPL in every resolved block. The honest one-line summary is: NO MODEL IS SIGNIFICANTLY PREFERRED IN ANY BLOCK; the burst is well described by a simple curved continuum throughout.
census_prior.class: SIMPLE-CONTINUUM NULL: no significant blackbody (union rule 0/6), no significant second break (max LRT_DSBPL_SBPL = 6.00 < 9.2), no model preferred by >= 10 AIC anywhere; a moderately hard, hard-to-soft single pulse with alpha above the synchrotron line of death in 4 of 5 resolved blocks. CAVEATS: (a) the archival window is 16 s SHORTER than the stamp, so the softest part of the burst was never fitted; (b) it predates the L8/L9 engine hardening, so the two-break result is a LOWER LIMIT and blocks 0/1 sit at ~60% of threshold; (c) blk4's DSBPL is invalid with xb railed at the 10 keV floor.

For the corresponding peak flux spectrum of each burst, we additionally required +1>=alpha>-0.45 and -1.7>beta>-3.3. These criteria yielded a sample of 41 GRBs.' OUR BURST PASSES ALL FOUR: fluence 2.30e-5; flnc alpha -0.470, beta -2.543; pflx alpha -0.209, beta -2.633.

SS2 verbatim (the rejection rule): 'we then examined whether the majority of the time-resolved bins within the T70 interval satisfy the same criteria applied to the peak spectrum. If at least ~80% of the bins in the T70 region met these conditions, the GRB was deemed suitable...' - our burst did NOT meet it. T70 = the interval between the 15% and 85% levels of the cumulative background-subtracted counts of the brightest detector.

Method frame: 3ML; three brightest NaI with source angle < 60 deg + brightest BGO; NaI 8-900 keV with 30-40 keV EXCLUDED (iodine K-edge, Bissaldi+2009); BGO 250 keV - 30 MeV; Bayesian-block bins (Scargle 2013) from the brightest NaI/BGO; polynomial background before and after the source interval.
